inline_comments.comment: `buildManualCommand` for the Claude path omits the effort flag. If a user runs in `--manual` mode with `--effort max`, the printed Claude CLI command won't include it. The Codex path correctly includes `--reasoning-effort ${variant.effort}`. For Claude, append `--effort ${variant.effort}` so the manual instructions are reproducible.

Same issue as `claude-code.ts`: no validation that `OPENAI_API_KEY` (or whatever key `@openai/codex-sdk` requires) is present before constructing `new Codex()`. Add an explicit guard that throws a descriptive `Error` naming the variable before the SDK call.

`AGENTS.claude.defaultEffort` is `'medium'` but the Zod schema in `eval.ts` defaults Claude's effort to `'high'`. The `defaultEffort` field in this config object is never read by `eval.ts` — the CLI default comes from the Zod schema. The inconsistency (and `config.test.ts` asserting `defaultEffort: 'medium'`) will confuse future contributors. Either remove `defaultEffort` from `AgentDefinition`/`AGENTS` if it isn't consumed anywhere, or align it with the Zod default and add a reference in `eval.ts`.

The function name `truncateEnd` is misleading: the implementation *keeps* the tail (`text.slice(-maxChars)`) and discards the beginning. From the caller's perspective, it truncates the start. Better names: `truncateStart`, `keepTail`, or `trimFromStart`. The comment says "snapping to a line boundary" — also worth noting it snaps to the *next* newline within the tail, not the last newline in the original text.

`promptName || 'setup'` uses `||` which silently replaces an explicitly passed empty string with `'setup'`. Per project rules, use `??` for config/option defaults: `promptName ?? 'setup'`. Same pattern appears at line 47 in the `generateTrialId` call.

The project's spy-mocking convention (`.cursor/rules/spy-mocking.mdc`) requires `vi.mock('module', { spy: true })` rather than the factory-replacement form `vi.mock('./prepare-trial', () => ({ prepareTrial: vi.fn() }))`. The factory form is reserved for modules that cannot be imported at all. `prepare-trial`, `grade`, and the agent modules here can all be imported — switch to `{ spy: true }` and configure mock behavior in `beforeEach` blocks via `vi.mocked(...).mockResolvedValue(...)`.

The module-level imports at the top (`import { computeQualityScore, ... } from './grade'`) precede the JSDoc block on line 14 that explains this file's purpose. The JSDoc should be at the very top of the file (before imports) or converted to a regular block comment above the first describe — as-is, it reads as a floating comment unattached to any export.

The `description` field is typed as `description?: string` (optional) but every entry provides one and `projects.test.ts` asserts `description: expect.any(String)`. Make it required (`description: string`) to match actual usage and make the test assertion enforceable at the type level.

On the first run, the code clones to `repoRoot` (inside the trial dir), installs deps, then copies to `cacheDir`. If the install step fails mid-way, `cacheDir` will be empty (`existsSync(join(cacheDir, '.git'))` returns false), so the next run will re-clone — that's fine. However, if the `cp repoRoot → cacheDir` call is interrupted after a successful install, subsequent runs will try to clone again (re-running a potentially slow install). Consider writing a sentinel file to `cacheDir` only after the full copy succeeds, to avoid a partial-cache state.

The `while (true)` loop in `resolveInstallRoot` relies on two exit conditions: `hasAnyMarker(current)` and `parent === current` (filesystem root). If neither fires before the boundary check and no marker is found, the function returns `start` — but only after walking to the filesystem root. Consider restructuring with an explicit `do...while (current !== parent)` loop to make the termination condition obvious, and add an early return when `current === boundary && !hasAnyMarker(current)` to avoid unnecessary upward traversal.

`citty` is added as a dependency but is not imported or used anywhere in the eval harness or any other script in this diff. Remove it to avoid dead weight in the dependency graph. (Confirmed: no file in the diff imports from `citty`.)

The `generate-and-run-config` executor resource class is bumped from `small` to `large` with no explanation in the PR description or as a comment here. `large` costs significantly more per CI minute. Please add a comment explaining why `small` was insufficient (e.g., OOM, timeout), and confirm this bump is intentional and not a leftover from debugging.

The import path uses an explicit `.ts` extension: `'./component-analyzer.ts'`. This is consistent with the migration toward native Node TS execution documented in `AGENTS.md`, but it's being introduced selectively — other imports in this file (e.g., from `storybook/internal/babel`, `glob`) keep their current form. Add a brief inline comment here (matching the pattern in `code/tsconfig.json`) explaining this is part of the `jiti` → native-node migration, so reviewers don't mistake it for a typo.

The test asserts Claude's pricing is `{}` (empty) only implicitly — the `toMatchObject` check on lines 17-29 doesn't validate `pricing` at all. If someone accidentally adds a (wrong) pricing table for Claude in the future, no test will catch it. Consider adding `expect(AGENTS.claude.pricing).toEqual({})` explicitly, with a comment explaining Claude reports cost natively via SDK.

general_comments.comment: `eval-parallel.ts` is referenced prominently in the PR description as a core piece of the architecture ("eval-parallel.ts — all 8 combos: node scripts/eval/eval-parallel.ts -p mealdrop") but is absent from this diff. The PR is incomplete as described. Either include `eval-parallel.ts` or remove the references to it from the PR description.

The `self-heal` prompt is cited in the PR description as one of the two prompt variants (`setup` (default), `self-heal` (vitest-based iteration loop)`) but no `scripts/eval/prompts/self-heal.md` file appears in the diff. The `listPrompts()` utility will return only `['setup']`, and passing `--prompt self-heal` at the CLI will throw `"Prompt not found"`. Either add the file or remove the reference.

`EVAL_ROOT` is resolved to a sibling directory outside the monorepo (`resolve(REPO_ROOT, '..', 'storybook-eval')`). This is undocumented in `AGENTS.md` or the PR description. Developers cloning fresh will have no `storybook-eval/` directory and may be confused when trial results silently accumulate outside the repo. Consider either documenting this layout in `AGENTS.md` or in a README under `scripts/eval/`, or defaulting to a path inside the repo (e.g., `scripts/eval/.cache`, `scripts/eval/results`) and adding both to `.gitignore` (which already covers `scripts/eval/.cache` and `scripts/eval/results` from the `.gitignore` hunk — but those paths wouldn't match an external `EVAL_ROOT`).

The `AGENTS.claude.defaultEffort` field ('medium') is inconsistent with the Zod schema default in `eval.ts` ('high'), and the `defaultEffort` field is never read by `eval.ts` to actually drive defaults. The `AgentDefinition` interface documents `defaultModel`/`defaultEffort` as if they're authoritative, but `eval.ts` defines its own defaults independently in the Zod schema. Either: (a) have `eval.ts` derive its defaults from `AGENTS[id].defaultEffort` and `AGENTS[id].defaultModel`, or (b) remove these fields from `AgentDefinition` and document that defaults live in the Zod schema.

The eval harness adds `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk@^0.2.85` and `@openai/codex-sdk@^0.117.0` — both at pre-1.0 or early versions where breaking changes may land in minor/patch bumps. Per project rules, before merging a dep bump, verify the changelog for breaking changes and confirm no local build issues. Also verify that named exports the code depends on (e.g., `query` from `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk`, `Codex`/`ModelReasoningEffort` from `@openai/codex-sdk`) actually exist at the pinned versions.
